passages.text: Whatever you tell yourself, that you become. Almost the first words the great Buddha uttered were: “What you think, that you are; what you will think, that you will be.” If this is true, do not teach yourself that you are nothing, ay, that you cannot do anything unless you are helped by somebody who does not live here, but sits above the clouds. The result will be that you will be more and more weakened every day.
passages.note: Self-belief; how the stories we tell ourselves shape us

passages.text: If you are to be rational, be rational all along the line, and if not, allow others the same privilege which you ask for yourselves.
passages.note: Fairness and consistency when judging others' beliefs
